claims.text: Machine-learning-based optimization of SPS parameters can reduce the required sintering temperature.
Lower-temperature, machine-learning-optimized SPS can maintain adequate densification.
Lower-temperature, machine-learning-optimized SPS can maintain adequate mechanical properties.
Powder feedstocks of refractory high-entropy alloys are suitable for SPS consolidation.
An iterative machine-learning workflow can adjust SPS temperature, dwell time, pressure, and pulsed-current profiles in real time.
SPS can be conducted under vacuum for refractory high-entropy-alloy powder consolidation.
A moderate SPS pressure in the range of 30–50 MPa is comparable to typical SPS values.
The optimization should begin at temperatures 100–300 °C below conventional sintering norms.
Localized electrical current and Joule heating in SPS facilitate rapid diffusion at particle interfaces.
Rapid interfacial diffusion caused by localized current and Joule heating reduces the temperature required for densification.
SPS enhances mass transport through electric-field-induced mechanisms.
SPS enhances mass transport through pressure-driven mechanisms.
A machine-learning system can continuously learn from real-time SPS data and identify lower-temperature parameter sets that optimize densification.
The proposed method can reduce sintering temperature by 100–300 °C relative to conventional approaches.
The proposed lower-temperature process can produce near-full density.
The proposed lower-temperature process can avoid substantial microstructural degradation.
Conventional pressureless sintering or standard hot pressing typically requires 1400–1700 °C or more for dense ceramics or refractory alloys with equivalent properties.
Extremely refractory systems may still require high temperatures for full densification.
The achievable temperature reduction and retention of mechanical properties depend on composition and equipment.
